comparisons.peer_summary: Net charge-offs increased $1.2 billion to $3.7 billion in 2024 compared to 2023, while loans 30 days or more past due increased $219 million and those 90 days or more past due increased $177 million at December 31, 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America report deteriorating credit quality metrics in their consumer lending portfolios for 2024, specifically highlighting increases in delinquency rates and net losses. Citi attributes the rise in its Mexico Consumer net credit loss rate and 90+ days past due delinquency rate to the normalization from post-pandemic lows. Similarly, BAC reports that its net charge-offs increased significantly in 2024 compared to 2023, alongside increases in loans 30 days or more past due and those 90 days or more past due, indicating a broader industry trend of rising credit costs in consumer portfolios.

sentences.text: As presented in the chart above, the fourth quarter of 2024 net credit loss rate and the 90+ days past due delinquency rate in Mexico Consumer increased quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year, primarily driven by the ongoing normalization of loss and delinquency rates from post-pandemic lows.
Net charge-offs increased $1.2 billion to $3.7 billion in 2024 compared to 2023.
Credit card loans 30 days or more past due increased $219 million, and 90 days or more past due increased $177 million at December 31, 2024.

comparisons.peer_summary: Provision for credit losses increased to $1.54 billion in 2024 from $1.14 billion in 2023, primarily driven by net charge-offs in the credit card portfolio.
comparisons.comparison: Goldman Sachs and Citi both identify increases in credit loss provisions and net charge-offs as key drivers of financial performance in their respective credit card portfolios for 2024. Citi's disclosure notes an increase in the net credit loss rate in its Mexico Consumer segment due to normalization, while GS explicitly states that the increase in its provision for credit losses to $1.54 billion was primarily driven by net charge-offs in its credit card portfolio. Both disclosures confirm rising credit costs in consumer credit products.

comparisons.peer_topic: Credit card portfolio growth and delinquency trends
comparisons.peer_summary: Total credit card loans increased year-over-year due to new accounts and revolving balances. Delinquency rates for 30+ and 90+ days both rose in 2024 compared to 2023, consistent with company expectations.
comparisons.comparison: JPMorgan Chase and Citi both report rising delinquency rates in their consumer credit portfolios for 2024. Citi highlights increased 90+ days past due delinquency rates in its Mexico Consumer segment, while JPMorgan reports that its 30+ and 90+ day delinquency rates for credit cards both rose in 2024 compared to 2023. Both companies frame these increases as consistent with expectations or normalization trends rather than unexpected adverse shocks.

sentences.text: As presented in the chart above, the fourth quarter of 2024 net credit loss rate and the 90+ days past due delinquency rate in Mexico Consumer increased quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year, primarily driven by the ongoing normalization of loss and delinquency rates from post-pandemic lows.

The December 31, 2024 30+ and 90+ day delinquency rates of 2.17% and 1.14%, respectively, increased compared to the December 31, 2023 30+ and 90+ day delinquency rates of 2.14% and 1.05%, respectively, in line with the Firm's expectations.
